subject: general
question: A and B together can do a piece of the work in 50 hours, B and C together can do the same work in 75 hours and A and C together can do the same in 25 hours. Find the time in which A, B, and C together will complete the task.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = **LCM** of (50, 75, 25) = 150 units.

Combined Efficiency 2(A + B + C) = (150/50) + (150/75) + (150/25) = 3 + 2 + 6 = 11.

Efficiency of (A + B + C) = 11/2.

Required Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 150 ÷ (11/2) = 300/11 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 300/11 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by (A + B) = 50 hours

Time taken by (B + C) = 75 hours

Time taken by (A + C) = 25 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Time × Efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of efficiencies = (A + B) + (B + C) + (A + C) = 3 + 2 + 6

⇒ 2(A + B + C) = 11

⇒ (A + B + C) Efficiency = 11/2

⇒ Time taken by (A + B + C) = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time = 150 ÷ (11/2)

⇒ Time = 300/11 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 300/11 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Combined Efficiency Rule

When individuals work in pairs, the sum of their individual efficiencies is half of the sum of the pair efficiencies: Efficiency(A+B+C) = [Eff(A+B) + Eff(B+C) + Eff(C+A)] ÷ 2.

Individual Time Calculation

To find A's time alone, subtract (B+C) efficiency from (A+B+C) efficiency and then divide Total Work by the result.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **Efficiency** of the workers if they work for the same duration.</p
